issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Mesh: proxy solicitation is not functional
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Mesh device with enabled On Demand proxy server cannot receive Proxy solicitation frames.
Also, On Demand proxy server and client parts have the compile time interdependencies that do not allow to work them independently.

Affects: MESH/SR/MPXS/BV-12-C

**To Reproduce**
Run the failed PTS test according to Zephyr documentation

**Expected behavior**
Mesh device could recognize Mesh Proxy Solicitation uuid, decrypt it correctly and should start sending proxy frame according to configured On Demand proxy state. PTS test should pass.

**Impact**
Qualification of Mesh v1.1 specification

review_comments: Elsewhere in the host I think we've tried to use WARN log level for potentially invalid external data, whereas ERR is reserved for local failures. Is there a good reason to use DBG instead of WARN here (and elsewhere in the file)?
Correction, WRN level (we used to have `BT_WARN()` but now it's `LOG_WRN()`.

Actually, it shouldn't happen because it is pre-parsed here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/adv.c#L338-L346
IMHO this checking is redundant at all. However, this is bugfix not feature refactoring.
Sure, but I don't think the log level changes are needed for the fix, right? They could be in a different commit or PR.

They are very useful. Right now, without added debug messages, mesh device just silently ignores everything what PTS toolchain sends to it even I enable debugging of proxy, models etc.
If you insist, I'll add them as a separate commit in this PR. The maintenance and bugfixing of proxy solicitation functionality are much complex without them.
